title: Luxury Lounge Material Stylist
description: The user is presented with a velvet sofa and a coffee mug in a stylish lounge setting. They must act as an interior material stylist, applying and fine-tuning physically-based materials on both objects through a multi-step interactive panel, adjusting roughness, metalness, color, emissive glow, and clearcoat properties to match a target luxury aesthetic shown as a reference swatch.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads GlamVelvetSofa.glb and coffeeMug.glb using GLTFLoader. Position the sofa at center and the mug on a small invisible platform near the sofa armrest as if placed on it. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (3, 2.5, 4) looking at origin. Add an HDR-style lighting rig: one warm DirectionalLight, one cool RimLight from behind, and a soft AmbientLight. Add a neutral gradient background using scene.background with a Color. Implement OrbitControls with damping enabled. Build an HTML overlay panel on the right side with these interactive controls, each requiring validation: (1) A dropdown to select the target object: Sofa or Mug. (2) A color picker that sets the base color (material.color) of the selected object's MeshStandardMaterial. (3) A roughness slider (0.0-1.0) that updates material.roughness in real time. (4) A metalness slider (0.0-1.0) that updates material.metalness. (5) An emissive color picker plus an emissive intensity slider (0.0-2.0) that sets material.emissive and material.emissiveIntensity. (6) A clearcoat slider (0.0-1.0) and clearcoat roughness slider (0.0-1.0) that require converting the material to MeshPhysicalMaterial if not already, setting material.clearcoat and material.clearcoatRoughness. Display a target reference swatch in the top-right corner showing a deep burgundy velvet sofa (color #6B1030, roughness 0.85, metalness 0.05, emissive #1A0008 at 0.3 intensity) and a glossy ceramic mug (color #F5F0E8, roughness 0.15, metalness 0.1, clearcoat 0.9). Add a Check Match button that compares current material parameters against the target values with a tolerance of 0.1 for each numeric parameter and a hex distance threshold of 40 for colors. Display a match percentage and show a success message when all parameters for both objects are within tolerance. Traverse loaded models to find all meshes and store references for material manipulation. Ensure material.needsUpdate is set when properties change. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop.
